verified.exploit_entry_point: Each adapter's own Builder + MakeRequests (the construction the exchange performs for POST /openrtb2/auction, /openrtb2/amp and /openrtb2/video). Hidden tests load the endpoint template from static/bidder-info and drive MakeRequests with a bid request whose imp.ext.bidder carries the attacker value, then assert no outbound request and a client-visible error.

traps.shape: the reported mechanism across the host-named published builders (subdomain and full-authority positions) with the shapes that actually move the authority (path, query, fragment, userinfo), plus the coupled legitimate values (mixed case, explicit ports, loopback and single-label names) that an over-broad fix rejects
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the reported example is one builder, so a fix aimed at that builder (or at one delimiter) looks sufficient while several spellings and the full-authority position remain open

traps.shape: a builder that never resolves the endpoint templates at all: it parses the configured URL, splits the host on '.', replaces the first label with the request value and reassembles, so a value containing a path separator rewrites the authority
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the report and every other site revolve around interpolated endpoint templates; this builder is a hand-rolled host rewrite in a separate package, and a fix centralised in the template resolution path never sees it
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the second implementation the published fix had to patch separately

traps.shape: the authorities of three published builders are fed by parameters whose names are not host-like (account, zone, and an optional zone identifier), so a search keyed on host fields misses them; one of them is legitimately empty and must stay empty
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the reported field is a host; these read as account and zone identifiers, and the empty-value case makes a naive check fail legitimate traffic

traps.shape: two real builders interpolate a request value into the authority but perform no shape check of their own; their only restriction is an enum in the parameter schema, a producer the builder never consults, so any caller that reaches the builder without that schema (or any future widening of the enum) gets an attacker-controlled destination
traps.reason_to_dismiss: both parameters are enum-constrained in the bundled schema and the builders only check for presence, so the schema looks like the protection and these two look different from the builders the report names
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the published fix leaves both builders untouched and relies on the schema enum

traps.shape: the existing host validation accepts the four configured shard names and additionally any value that ends in the vendor domain; the branch reads as support for fully-qualified shard names, and a value whose path separator sits before that suffix still rewrites the authority
traps.reason_to_dismiss: there is a validation function with an explicit allowlist; the extra suffix branch looks like an intentional compatibility feature, so the adapter appears protected
traps.realistic_because: injected sibling a maintainer could plausibly have written while adding regional shards; the adapter is untouched by the published fix

traps.shape: the region for the outbound host is extracted from a request-supplied route URL and checked against an allowlist, but a compatibility branch accepts an explicit region from the route query when the host label is absent, without any check, so a value with a path separator reaches the authority
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the allowlisted extraction from the route hostname reads as the guard, and the fallback is a small compatibility branch in the same function
traps.realistic_because: injected sibling a maintainer could plausibly have written for partners whose routes lack the regional host label; the adapter is untouched by the published fix
